en1|summary|57e0a38b8db450efe897fe42a7c6.text:
Can an Agent clone any software without source code?

Length: 4,453 characters. Reading time: about 15 minutes.

Over the past couple of days, a project called REA (Reverse Engineer Anything) has blown up on GitHub. How big? As of October 12, its repo page showed 120,000 stars. For comparison, OpenClaw, which kicked off the nationwide lobster-farming craze earlier this year and delivered miraculous growth, had accumulated 60,000 new stars by its third day of breakout.

Project URL: https://github.com/morluto/rea

What it does, in the GitHub README's own words, is: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries. In short, it uses AI coding agents such as Claude Code and Codex, connected via MCP to reverse-engineering tools like Ghidra and Hopper, to let the Agent analyze software without source code, trace clues about how a feature is implemented, and based on

en1|summary|60abd382f9d37f77f4d7d6cb384b.text:
Claude Code, Cursor, and Codex can do the same job and still pick completely different tools.

Word count: 3,079 words | Reading time: about 10 minutes

AI's influence has pushed attention from search engine optimization (SEO) to answer engine optimization (AEO) — optimizing content so it can be served up as an answer generated by an Agent. One step beyond that is generative engine optimization (GEO), where brands try to shape what LLMs say.

Is software tooling itself about to get reshuffled too, with coding assistants like Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor leaning toward one particular debugging suite, pentesting tool, migration tool, package manager, database (or any other core piece of the stack you can think of)?
